content.comment_body: Hello everyone, We use several [product_name] controllers in our family business. I am considering using a [product_name] HMI device to visualize and control our automation tasks involving multiple [product_name] controllers. 1. Is it possible to connect and configure the HMI for use with [product_name]? 2. Is an additional communication module required to serve as a gateway between the different controller series? Best regards, [user_name]
Hi, If the HMI supports communication protocols like TCP/IP or Modbus TCP/IP, it should be compatible. Please consult the HMI manual for details. Hope this helps.

Hello [user_name], Welcome to the forum. 1) You can visualize data from multiple [product_name] controllers using the HMI. 2) No additional communication module is needed, but note that a basic HMI can only connect directly to up to 4 [product_name] controllers. For more than 4 devices, you will need to aggregate data, for example, in one controller.
Thank you. I will look into the documentation and check.

Thank you for the information. Initially, we plan to connect exactly 4 [product_name] controllers. With the HMI, can I assign virtual touch buttons to the inputs in my [product_name] program? Also, when is the [product_name] Communication Module required? Is it needed if I want to integrate the [product_name] network with other controller networks?

Yes, you can set up virtual buttons for actions like switching. However, you cannot use them to operate physical inputs directly on the [product_name] controller. The [product_name] Communication Module is necessary only if you wish to connect the controller to a KNX bus system. For connecting a [product_name] with other controllers, devices with compatible industrial network protocols are needed. See further information at [url].

analysis.insight_summary: The user explored using an HMI to connect and control multiple automation controllers, seeking direct connectivity and the ability to assign virtual buttons to program inputs. Responses clarified direct connection limits (up to 4 controllers), when communication modules are needed, and addressed misconceptions about controlling inputs. There is some confusion on specific system capabilities and network integration options.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects straightforward integration and control between the HMI and multiple controllers, including virtual input assignment and scalability for expanding the network. They hope to limit extra hardware requirements and want clearer guidance on integration procedures.
